A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IDArb. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original intrinsic-decomposition experiments, ablations, photometric-stereo results and inverse-rendering evaluations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and adds qualitative MIT-Intrinsic comparisons in Appendix D, Figure 11.

M1.justification: The diffusion architecture, cross-view and cross-component attention, illumination augmentation, alternating single/multiple-input training, noise schedule and downstream procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training datasets and evaluation coverage are retained. MIT-Intrinsic and Stanford-ORB were already evaluated in v1 Appendix D; v2's new MIT-Intrinsic illustrations do not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the reported evaluations. IntrinsicAnything, shown in v2's new MIT-Intrinsic figure, was already the comparator for that benchmark in v1 Table 8.

E3.justification: Reported training budgets, view sampling, evaluation resolution, metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. The contrast adjustment noted in v2 Figure 11 concerns display visibility, not a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The attention and training ablations, viewpoint/lighting analysis, failure cases and scene-generalization tests are retained. The new MIT-Intrinsic figure illustrates an existing benchmark comparison without adding a separate diagnostic or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version provides experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, error bars or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-9 are retained. v2 adds four qualitative MIT-Intrinsic albedo comparisons showing inputs, IntrinsicAnything, IDArb and ground truth in Figure 11; these are additional visual results, not numerical performance gains.

T1.justification: The conditional-generation formulation and Appendix A's diffusion and rendering mathematics, including Equations 1-3, are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about arbitrary-view decomposition, varying illumination, consistency, the dataset and downstream applications. Minor caption wording changes do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning material ambiguity, synthetic-data simplification, scene/text failures and quadratic attention cost remain unchanged. The new reference to Appendix F points to existing failure-case discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, training-time and dataset-construction information is unchanged. The existing project URL moves from the author header to the abstract without changing resource-access information.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work positioning are unchanged. Newly prominent references to MIT-Intrinsic and Stanford-ORB concern works already cited and evaluated in v1.

P1.justification: v2 updates author affiliations and contact information, adds an acknowledgement, relocates the project link and makes limited caption and cross-reference edits. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-row MIT-Intrinsic Figure 11, renumbers subsequent appendix figures, and relocates retained displays including Tables 1 and 3 and Figure 8. Caption, spacing and pagination changes are limited.

improvement.justification: v1 provides MIT-Intrinsic summary scores in Table 8; v2 adds baseline, prediction and ground-truth examples in Figure 11, with display adjustments disclosed. These let readers inspect residual shading and lost detail directly. Clearer references to existing benchmarks and failure cases also help navigation. The gains are modest because the method, quantitative evidence and limitations are unchanged.
